sections.title: Imports the building blocks
sections.what: Brings in the tools the page needs: the startup hook, the notification library, the main Dashboard, and the shared store.

sections.name: App
sections.title: Main app screen and startup load
sections.what: Builds the whole page. It loads the default inputs once when the page opens, styles the pop-ups (dark background, green for success, red for error), places the Dashboard, and shows a bottom-right error box when the store holds an error.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping every global piece in one place gives the app one error box and one notification style.
sections.watch_out: The startup load depends on loadDefaults being a stable function; if it changed on every render, the defaults would reload repeatedly.

summary: The top-level shell of the web app: it loads the default inputs when the page opens, shows pop-up notifications, and displays any global error held by the shared store.
purpose: Gives the whole page one starting point, combining the Dashboard, the notification area, and a box for global errors.
why: Likely reason: loading the default inputs once at startup means the input form is filled in when the user first arrives.
how: When the page first appears, it asks the shared store to load the default inputs. It then draws the notification area and the Dashboard. If the store holds an error, it also draws a red error box in the bottom-right corner.
inputs: The loadDefaults action and the error value from the store. The file takes no direct user input.
outputs: The page frame, success and error pop-ups, and the error box when the store reports an error.
risks: If loading defaults fails, the failure is logged to the console. The user sees it in the error box only if the store also saves the error. Pop-ups close after 4 seconds.
debug: If the form opens empty, check loadDefaults in the store and look for a logged error in the browser console. If the red error box stays after a successful action, check that the store clears its error value.
